findings.issue: Ownership-capture bypass: editing a foreign ci/checks/*.sh AND rewriting its second line to '# T-<own-task> ·' (or DELETE+re-ADD same name with own header) yields exit 0 PASS, fully neutering the foreign invariant. Reproduced in isolated tmp git repos (PROBE 2/3). The script reads the owner header from the ON-DISK (post-edit) version, which the attacker controls, instead of from the BASE_REF version.
findings.suggestion: For files present in BASE_REF (diff-filter C/M/R/T), determine the owner T-ID from the BASE_REF version via `git show BASE_REF:path | sed -n '2p'` (as already done for deletes), NOT from the on-disk file. Rewriting the owner header of an existing foreign check then becomes a forbidden ownership change.

findings.issue: Branch-name-spoof bypass: a branch named task/T-0044-anything sets TASK_ID=T-0044 and is then permitted to edit/gut the real T-0044 check (dual-control-isolation.sh) → exit 0 PASS. Reproduced (PROBE 5). TASK_ID derives solely from the agent-controlled branch name with no independent anchor. Not listed in spec Out-of-scope §7 nor ADR §7; the ADR/spec contain no 'erring-agent-not-adversary' threshold statement (grep confirmed).
findings.suggestion: Either (a) fixing R-1 via BASE_REF header already closes the edit-by-spoof path, or (b) explicitly accept this in ADR §7 with rationale (rely on reviewer seeing the header diff), which would downgrade it to nit. Currently undocumented => blocking.

findings.issue: Destructive shrink of ci/checks/known_tenant_tables.txt (removing a registry line) passes (exit 0). Spec FR-6.2 promises 'additive edits' are fine but the gate ignores the .txt entirely, so destructive edits also pass.
findings.suggestion: Accepted by design (.txt is out of the *.sh glob, spec §7). Note as residual risk; no change required for this gate.

findings.issue: Removing a foreign check's invocation from the fitness chain in package.json disables it as effectively as gutting it, and is not caught (out of ci/checks/*.sh glob).
findings.suggestion: Accepted by design (spec §7 scopes gate to ci/checks/*.sh). Candidate for a separate fitness-chain-integrity gate; not in this task's scope.

role_gap_evidence: Integrity meta-gates must anchor ownership in something NOT controlled by the audited agent (BASE_REF header or control-plane claim). T-0146 proves both control-strings (branch name + file line 2) are agent-controlled => self-declaring ownership is trivially bypassable (PROBE 3/5). Candidate for ledgers/role-gaps.md.
The AC set itself is incomplete for the goal stated in spec §2 ('make CI-weakening visible before PR'): no AC covers header-rewrite or branch-spoof, so the spec under-specified the threat surface.
